predecessors.name: Kingdom of Kush
predecessors.text: Lower Nubia from the first cataract to the third; the Nobatae 'had been invited into the region from the Western Desert by the Roman Emperor Diocletian in 297 AD'

successors.name: Makuria
successors.text: the whole kingdom, 'annexed by their southern neighbor, Makuria'

ledger.x: 347: the Nobatae hold Lower Nubia after Kush.

c. 450: Silko drives the Blemmyes from the Nile. Infobox '450 A.D: Silko (first known king)'; the page does not date the war; the Blemmyes page: 'By the late 4th century they had occupied Lower Nubia and established a kingdom' with 'Kalabsha... the capital of the Blemmyes' and cities at Faras, Ballana and Aniba, and…

certainty.note: The northern frontier at Philae is Rome's treaty line from Diocletian's settlement of 297 and is sharp in effect; the southern frontier with Makuria (second or third cataract, Batn el-Hajar) and the desert edges are soft.
